relatedSnapshot.title: Charged $99/month for a Whitelabel Partner subscription while the app shows the Free plan (Intercom: <email>)
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

**Source**: Intercom contact <email> ("Name 9", free workspace, plan shows Free).

**Ask (bucket: overcharged)**: "I've been getting charged $99 since June even though I'm on the free plan." Manage Billing shows no invoices; Current Plan = Free; no credits, no managed domains or inboxes. A bank screenshot shows the descriptor "Whop\*acquisity" for $99.

**Finding**: The $99/month charge is a real, still-active Whitelabel Partner subscription bought on 2026-06-27 through Acquisity's own Whop store (product route acq-whitelabel-partner-iz3, plan slot partner_subscription), under the buyer account <email>. Whop payments of $99 succeeded on 2026-06-27, 2026-07-27, 2026-08-26 and 2026-09-25 (four cycles, $396 charged, nothing refunded, no dispute). The purchase provisioned the partner "Name 7" (self-serve) and the workspace "Name 8", which the customer is not signed into and has never used (no client workspace, no plans, no campaign). The workspace he wrote from is a different, free workspace, so the app correctly shows Free with no invoices: the workspace plan and the Whop partner subscription are separate billing layers on separate accounts.

**Exposure**: $396.00 charged across four cycles; a fifth $99 charge is due around 2026-10-25 unless the subscription is cancelled. Nothing refunded to date.

**Proposed human action (not a promise)**: A person with access to the partner billing account should confirm with the customer whether he intended to buy the Whitelabel Partner subscription, then either keep it and explain the separate billing layer, or cancel the Whop membership and refund the unused cycles it never delivered. No customer self-service fix exists because the paid subscription lives on a different account and is billed outside the app.

**Unconfirmed**: Autumn plan/add-on state for the paid partner account (it is partner-governed and has no Acquisity Autumn customer), and the customer's intent.

3 months free Acquisity membership (hoping for 12 months free)

#### What are you doing to achieve it?

Client has been complaining for weeks, stating that the sales rep (Name 12) told him that there would be no future costs and that the DFY sales deck shows that our AI proprietary system is included in the membership. This is not a matter of cost. It is a matter of integrity and trust between what was portrayed in the sales process and what is actually being delivered in the program.

He would like his first 12 months of his membership - Acquisity for free, as stated on the sales call and in the DFY sales deck.

12 months free but he's willing to start with 3 months free for now but it doesn't feel good to him and he's losing trust in us. I would personally recommend just giving him 12 months but let me know what Jared says. He is looking to upsell if we get him results and things are moving along.
